docs.title: HeLab
docs.text:
HeLab, the Helium Experiment Lab Analysis Board, is a desktop app for analysing a helium BEC experiment's delay-line-detector (DLD) data as it comes in. It browses the lab's data folders, loads and caches each shot's TXY events, follows a folder live as new shots arrive, converts raw detector files to TXY, and runs analysis scripts as interactive plots.

It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• New to HeLab? Install it and open your first folder.
  • Doing something specific? The how-to guides cover marking a data root so HeLab can cache a folder on disk, following a folder live, converting raw files to TXY and writing your own analysis script.
  • Looking something up? See the command line, the settings, the .hlb file format and the API for script writers.
  • Want to know why it works the way it does? Read how HeLab caches data.

docs.title: A few things HeLab always does
docs.text:
• It never changes or deletes your raw data files or existing TXY files. It writes into a data folder only the .helab-root marker you ask for and, if you turn it on for that folder, converted TXY files.
  • It never reads a file that is still being written: a file modified within the last few seconds waits until it settles.
  • It never removes your cached data, settings or presets without asking, apart from the routine tidying described in how HeLab caches data.

docs.title: HeLab's .hlb files
docs.text: HeLab's disk cache (store-v4) keeps its binary data in .hlb files. This page describes the format and how to read one with or without HeLab, from the command line, and from MATLAB. HeLab writes .hlb files from version 0.0.8, which turns store-v4 on; earlier versions write none. HeLab's code: helab.utils.hlb.read, helab.convert.raw_layer.columns, helab.convert.txy_layer.unpack_segment, and helab cache dump|export (helab/cache_cli.py). The "without HeLab" sample below runs as a test (tests/test_cache_cli.py), checked against a file HeLab wrote.

docs.title: What a .hlb file is
docs.text: HeLab's disk cache (store-v4) keeps binary data in .hlb files: named NumPy arrays, compressed, with a JSON header that says what they are and who made them. No Python pickle anywhere, so any language can read one. There are two kinds: a raw layer, one raw TDC file d<N>.txt parsed into its pulses (store-v4/raw/<uuid>.hlb), and a TXY segment, some shots of one folder's TXY layer (store-v4/txy/<uuid>.hlb).

docs.title: Byte layout (format 1)
docs.text:
Offset Size Field 0 8 magic 89 48 4C 42 0D 0A 1A 0A (\x89HLB\r\n\x1a\n; a text-mode copy or a cut file fails it) 8 4 header length L, unsigned little-endian (at most 16 MiB) 12 4 CRC32 (zlib's) of the header's bytes, unsigned little-endian 16 L header: JSON, UTF-8 16 + L to the end the arrays' compressed chunks, back to back, in the order the header lists them

The chunks tile the rest of the file exactly: no gap, no overlap, nothing after the last.

docs.title: The header
docs.text:
{
  "format": 1,
  "kind": "raw",
  "maker": {"maker": "<session id>", "record": {"helab_version": "…", "commit": "…", "hostname": "…", "…": "…"}},
  "meta": {"encoding": "i8-i64d-1", "parser": 1, "facts": {"rows": 41092, "t_zero": "13656646605557.0", "…": "…"},
           "name": "d1.txt"},
  "arrays": [
    {"name": "channel", "dtype": "|i1", "shape": [41092],
     "codec": {"name": "blosc", "cname": "zstd", "clevel": 9, "shuffle": "byte", "typesize": 1},
     "chunks": [{"offset": 0, "length": 12345, "size": 41092, "crc32": 305419896}]},
    {"name": "time", "dtype": "<i8", "shape": [41092], "codec": {"…": "…"}, "chunks": [{"…": "…"}]}
  ]
}
  • format: this layout's version. A reader refuses a higher one; it never rewrites a file.
  • kind: raw (a raw layer) or txy (a TXY segment).
  • maker: which HeLab session made the file: its id, and its record with HeLab's version and commit, the machine's random id, its hostname, and Python, NumPy, SciPy and blosc versions. A file shared off the machine carries the hostname.
  • meta: the kind's own fields (below).
  • arrays: each one's name; dtype in NumPy's spelling with explicit byte order (|i1, |u1, <i8, <f8, the only ones read today); shape; codec; and chunks. In each chunk, offset counts from the end of the header, length is its compressed bytes, size its uncompressed bytes (at most 64 MiB, cut at element boundaries) and crc32 is zlib's CRC32 of its compressed bytes.
  • Codec blosc: each chunk is one python-blosc (Blosc 1) frame, decompressed with blosc.decompress. cname and clevel are as written (raw layers: zstd 9). shuffle byte is Blosc's byte shuffle by typesize, undone by the decompressor itself.

docs.title: Raw layers (kind raw)
docs.text:
meta.encoding says which arrays the file holds:

  • i8-i64d-1 (the TDC's own files): channel (|i1) and time (<i8). The time is stored as row 0's time, then each row's difference from the one before, so numpy.cumsum(time) gives the absolute TDC times. Row order: the file's first row (the trigger, MATLAB's t_zero) comes first, then every other row sorted by time, with ties in file order. Every converter backend reads the pulses in this order and gives byte-identical TXY.
  • f64-1 (any other file: other line endings, NaN fields, decimals, …): channels and times (<f8), exactly as HeLab's reader parses the text, in file order, NaN where a field was empty.

Times are TDC bins. HeLab's profiles use 25 ps (bin_time 25e-12 s), so seconds = bins × 25e-12.

meta.facts holds what HeLab's done-writing checks read from the text: rows, t_zero (as text; "nan" for an empty file), first_channel, blank, final_newline, line_endings (crlf, lf, cr, mixed, none) and reader (strict or general), and stop_line: the line where the general reader stopped at a token it couldn't read, as MATLAB's converter stops (an integer from 1), or null when the file was read to its end; layers written before HeLab learnt it have no stop_line. meta.parser is HeLab's parser version (1).

docs.title: TXY layers (kind txy)
docs.text:
A folder's TXY data is kept per layer: matlab (MATLAB's TXY) or helab:<profile hash> (one per HeLab profile's content hash; its tags, such as m19v1 and p22v1, are names for it). Each layer is a set of append-only segments, each one .hlb holding some of the layer's shots; when a shot is in several, the newest segment wins (the store's rows say which segment holds each shot, so a lone segment may hold superseded shots).

Arrays:

  • shots (<i8 [k]): the shot numbers, ascending;
  • offsets (<i8 [k+1]): shot i's hits are rows offsets[i] to offsets[i+1] of hits;
  • hits (<f8 [N, 3]): T in s, X in m, Y in m, one hit per row;
  • problematic (|u1 [k]): 1 where the shot's TXY had empty fields or couldn't be read whole.

meta: layer, profile_hash ("" for matlab), tags, and precision: g8 holds the values the 8-significant-figure text parses to (MATLAB's TXY and m19v1, so a shot equals its text TXY), f64 full float64 (newer profiles). Codec: Blosc zstd 9 with no shuffle (shuffle none).

from helab.convert import txy_layer
shots, problematic, header = txy_layer.unpack_segment(open("seg.hlb", "rb").read())  # {shot: (n, 3) float64}

Without HeLab, read_hlb below gives the same arrays: hits[offsets[i]:offsets[i + 1]] is shot shots[i].

docs.title: The format rule
docs.text: An additive change keeps format 1: a new header field, a new meta field, a new array, a new kind, a new encoding name, or a new codec or dtype. Readers ignore fields they don't know, and refuse an array whose dtype or codec they don't know (an error, never a silent guess). Only a change to this byte layout, or to what an existing field means, raises format. An older HeLab meeting a newer format refuses the file and never rewrites, moves or deletes it.

docs.title: Python, with HeLab
docs.text:
from helab.utils import hlb
header, arrays = hlb.read("d1.hlb")               # every part checked; hlb.HlbError if not
from helab.convert import raw_layer
layer, header = raw_layer.from_hlb(open("d1.hlb", "rb").read())
columns = raw_layer.columns(layer)                # channel, time_bins (absolute), time_s
pulses = raw_layer.decode(layer)                  # or: .channels, .times (float64, TDC bins), as the converter reads them

docs.title: Python, without HeLab (NumPy and python-blosc only)
docs.text:
import json, struct, zlib
import blosc, numpy as np

def read_hlb(path):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    if data[:8] != b"\x89HLB\r\n\x1a\n":
        raise ValueError("not a .hlb file")
    length, crc = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, 8)
    header_bytes = data[16:16 + length]
    if zlib.crc32(header_bytes) != crc:
        raise ValueError("header damaged")
    header = json.loads(header_bytes)
    base, arrays = 16 + length, {}
    for entry in header["arrays"]:
        pieces = []
        for chunk in entry["chunks"]:
            packed = data[base + chunk["offset"]:base + chunk["offset"] + chunk["length"]]
            if zlib.crc32(packed) != chunk["crc32"]:
                raise ValueError(entry["name"] + ": chunk damaged")
            pieces.append(blosc.decompress(packed))
        arrays[entry["name"]] = np.frombuffer(b"".join(pieces), dtype=entry["dtype"]).reshape(entry["shape"])
    return header, arrays

header, arrays = read_hlb("d1.hlb")
if header["meta"]["encoding"] == "i8-i64d-1":
    channel, bins = arrays["channel"], np.cumsum(arrays["time"])
else:
    channel, bins = arrays["channels"], arrays["times"]
seconds = bins * 25e-12

Checked against a file HeLab wrote (tests/data/convert/cases/basic/d1.txt's layer): the same channels and times as raw_layer.decode.

docs.title: From the command line (read only)
docs.text:
helab cache dump d1.hlb                                   # the header as JSON (arrays without their chunk lists)
helab cache export d1.hlb --to npz|mat|csv [--out PATH]   # channel, time_bins, time_s, header
helab cache export --folder /data/2026-10-31/run --to mat # every raw layer store-v4 holds for that folder
helab cache export --folder /data/2026-10-31/run --kind txy [--layer matlab|m19v1|helab:<hash>] --to csv
helab cache export seg.hlb --to npz                      # a TXY segment: t_s, x_m, y_m and a shot column

A file's export goes to the current folder (d1.npz), a folder's to ./helab-export-<name>/d<N>.<ext> (with --kind txy, d_txy<N>.<ext>, one per shot, columns t_s, x_m, y_m, of the layer --layer names, by layer or tag, or the only one there is); nothing is replaced without --force, and nothing is ever written into a store. --bin-time changes the seconds per bin (raw layers).

docs.title: MATLAB
docs.text:
MATLAB has no Blosc reader, so export the file first: helab cache export d1.hlb --to mat writes a .mat with channel (int8), time_bins (absolute, int64), time_s (double) and header (the JSON text):

s = load('d1.mat');
plot(s.time_s(s.channel == 5), '.');   % the trigger channel's pulses
info = jsondecode(s.header);

docs.title: How HeLab caches data
docs.text:
HeLab keeps the data you load in two places: in RAM for this session, and in a disk cache on this computer so that a folder opens at once next time. This page explains both, the budgets that keep them in check, and what HeLab will and won't delete.

Caching never changes your data folders: your raw d files and TXY files are never touched by anything on this page.

docs.title: RAM and the disk cache
docs.text:
When you load a folder, its shots are held in RAM. If the folder is inside a data root, HeLab also saves them to the disk cache in the background. Without a data root the folder is RAM only: nothing about it is saved (see Mark a data root).

Next time you select a cached folder, its data shows straight away ("Cached data found" or "Cached data loaded"), while HeLab checks the folder for changes ("Checking for changes…"). If the folder wasn't modified, the check looks only at a few of its files; how many is Settings › General › Check of cached data (default Medium). Right-click a folder › Retry / Refresh to compare every file.

Besides each folder's TXY data, the disk cache keeps a copy of the raw pulses (filled in the background after a folder's data is cached), each folder's counts and status, and, if you turn on Settings › Cache › Reuse saved analysis results (off at first), the results of costly plots. Settings › Cache › Cache policy chooses what new saves keep: Raw + what you load (default), Raw only, convert on load, or TXY only (no raw). Changing it removes nothing. Right-click › Cache policy for this folder… sets it for one folder.

docs.title: Files still being written
docs.text: A file modified within the last few seconds may still be being written by the acquisition computer. HeLab never reads, caches or counts such a file; it picks it up on a later check. The time is Settings › General › Read files unmodified for: 5 s by default, from 2 to 60 s. Files dated in the future count as still being written too. The summary line shows "N still being written" while any are waiting.

docs.title: The disk budget
docs.text:
The disk cache has a budget: by default 8 GB on macOS and Linux, 8 GiB on Windows (at least 1 GB or 1 GiB). Set it in Settings › Cache, which also shows how much is used. It counts cached data, cached analysis and the records; data you removed doesn't count while it waits out its 10-minute grace period before deletion.

Near the budget, HeLab asks rather than deletes:

  • At 80 %, a "Disk cache nearly full" window appears once. Automatic loading of folders without cached data pauses ("Auto-load paused — disk cache 80% full"); cached folders still open, and right-click › Load data still works. Choose Open purge settings, or Ignore this time (it asks again if usage rises by another 10 % of the budget).
  • A save that doesn't fit asks "Disk cache full": Make room removes the least recently used cached data of other folders until it fits (the window says how much it removes), or Don't cache this folder now.
  • An update that grows a cached folder while the cache is 80 % full asks "Save the cache update?": Save update or Don't cache this update now.

Either way, the loaded data stays in RAM. HeLab asks one question at a time.

docs.title: The RAM budget
docs.text:
Settings › Cache › RAM budget is a share of the computer's RAM, in steps of 1/128: 1/8 by default, at least 1 GiB, at most half. When loaded folders go over it, HeLab drops those no tab is showing, least recently used first. Folders shown in tabs are never dropped, so HeLab can use more than the budget.

Plots count too. At 50 % of the budget the status bar says so; at 75 % a window lists the biggest plots and folders; above 80 % plots you haven't viewed lately are released: each keeps a picture of itself and draws again from RAM or the disk cache when you show it (Reload a released plot when it is shown again, on by default). HeLab never closes a plot, and never releases the shown, running or Live plot.

Large folders. Before loading, HeLab estimates a folder's size from its TXY files. Above the RAM budget or 10 % of RAM, a folder isn't loaded automatically: the line says "Large folder · ~X in RAM" with Load anyway… and No auto-load. Loading it anyway asks you to tick "I understand this may slow down or stop HeLab". Above 30 % of RAM it doesn't load.

docs.title: Your choices per folder
docs.text:
Right-click a folder for:

  • Don't cache this folder: its data stays in RAM only; its tooltip says "Not cached: your choice".
  • Don't auto-load this folder: selecting it no longer loads it; use Load data.

Each applies to that folder only, not its subfolders, and needs a data root. Clear all and purges keep them; Settings › Cache › Folder preferences › Clear… resets them.

docs.title: Clearing the cache
docs.text:
Everything below asks first and says what goes and what stays. Loaded data stays open.

  • Settings › Cache clears by kind (Cached data, Folder summaries, Scan failures, Subfolder status, Folder listings, Cached analysis, and the raw pulses and TXY data rows), or everything with Clear all… (which keeps cached analysis, folder preferences and presets). Remove old entries removes what you haven't used for a number of days.
  • Settings › Data roots › Clear cached data… clears one data root.
  • Right-click a folder › Clear loaded data cache clears that folder.

docs.title: What HeLab never deletes without asking
docs.text:
HeLab never removes your data, cached data, records, folder choices, folder constants or presets unless you ask. The only things it tidies by itself are:

  • files of cached data you removed or that a newer save replaced, after a grace period, and stray cache files no record refers to, once over an hour old;
  • saves still waiting for your answer (Make room), after an hour;
  • at startup, cache folders from older HeLab versions and log files beyond Log files to keep (Settings › General, 300 by default);
  • the oldest entries of lists kept only for this session;
  • loaded folders and plots, to stay within the RAM budget, as described above;
  • the converter's own unfinished temporary files, once over an hour old.

docs.title: The cache folder
docs.text:
Each computer has its own disk cache. By default it is in ~/Library/Caches/HeLab/caches on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeLab\caches on Windows and ~/.cache/HeLab/caches on Linux. Settings › Cache shows where, with Open.

To move it, use Settings › General › Cache folder › Change…. The new folder must be empty or new, writable, with enough free space, and not on a network drive or in a synced folder. HeLab pauses loading and folder checks while it moves, and keeps the cache's contents. If the move is interrupted, HeLab finishes or undoes it at the next start.

If the cache folder also holds an older HeLab's cache, the Older cache (store-v3) row in Settings › Cache lets you keep reading it, ignore it or clear it.

While File › Work Offline is on, HeLab browses and analyses cached data only, reading no data folder or server.

docs.title: Install and open your first folder
docs.text: This page takes you from nothing to a first plot of your data. You do it once; after that you only start HeLab.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
HeLab needs Python 3.13. The simplest way to get it is uv, which installs Python by itself: you don't need a system Python, conda or admin rights.

  1. Install uv (once per computer), then open a new terminal so uv is found:

    # macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

    # Windows
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

  2. Clone HeLab and create its Python 3.13 environment:

    git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TonyXTYan/HeLab.git
cd HeLab
uv python install 3.13
uv venv --seed --python 3.13 venv

  3. Activate the environment and install HeLab with the pinned versions:

    source venv/bin/activate       # macOS / Linux
venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows
uv pip install -r requirements.lock -e .

  4. Start it:

    helab

Next time, activate venv and run helab, or run venv/bin/helab (macOS and Linux) or venv\Scripts\helab (Windows) without activating.

Note

On a lab computer, a bare python may be a much older interpreter. Always use the one in venv. On Windows, start HeLab from the desktop, not over SSH: an administrator SSH session can leave cache folders that a normal start can't write to.

docs.title: Or download a release build
docs.text:
Each release on the releases page has a ready-built HeLab for macOS (HeLab.app), Windows and Linux. Download the archive for your system, unpack it and open HeLab. You don't need Python for a release build.

Only one HeLab runs on a computer at a time. If you start a second one, it says "HeLab is already running on this computer" and closes; use the window that is already open.

docs.title: Find your data folder
docs.text:
The window has three parts: the folder panel on the left, the plot area in the middle, and the plot settings and Scripts panel on the right. With nothing loaded, the plot area says "Select a data folder to begin".

To go to your data:

  • type its path in the box at the top of the folder tab (for example /Volumes/Data/2026/run 1 or D:\data\run1) and press Return, or
  • use File › Open, or
  • double-click folders in the tree. Up Dir in the left toolbar goes one level up, and New Tab opens another folder tab.

docs.title: Read the folder tree
docs.text:
The tree shows Name, Modified, Counts (shots found) and Status for each folder. Counts and status appear once a folder has been checked: select it, or use Check folder status in the left toolbar (its small arrow chooses folders in view, the current folder, or subfolders to a depth). View › Automatically Check Folder Status in View does this for you; it is off at first.

The status icon compares the raw d<N>.txt and TXY files in the folder:

  • a green tick: every shot has both its raw and its TXY file;
  • a yellow, amber or red icon: some shots have only one of the two (hover the row for details);
  • a grey circle with a dot: no data files here, but some subfolders have data;
  • a dashed circle: no data files here, and what its subfolders hold isn't known yet;
  • a small grey dot: no data here at all.

Small badges beside the status icon tell you more. The ones you meet first:

  • a green box: the folder's data is loaded in RAM;
  • a package: the folder's data is in the disk cache (with a clock: the folder may have changed since);
  • a blue anchor: the folder holds a .helab-root, so it and its subfolders can use the disk cache (see Mark a data root).

Hover any row for a tooltip that spells out what is known about it, and when.

docs.title: Load a folder's shots
docs.text:
Select a folder: HeLab loads its TXY files into RAM by itself (View › Toggle Auto Load to RAM turns this off). You can also right-click a folder and choose Load data.

The lines under the path box show the selected folder, how many TXY files were found and loaded, and the folder's cache state. Folder details, below the tree, shows a running load's progress and time left. Press Esc, or Cancel on that line, to stop a load.

If a folder is already in the disk cache, its data shows at once and the line says "Checking for changes…" while HeLab checks the folder.

docs.title: Open your first plot
docs.text: In the Scripts panel on the right, choose a group (for example Basic plots v1 or DLD Front Panel Port) and click Plot beside a script such as "Counts per shot". The plot opens in the middle, on the data the current tab has loaded; its settings show in the panel above the scripts. If no data is loaded yet, the status bar says "load a folder's data first".

docs.title: Convert raw files to TXY
docs.text:
HeLab has its own TXY converter. It turns the delay-line detector's raw files, d<N>.txt, into TXY files of hits (time and X, Y position), named d_txy_helab_<tag>_<N>.txt. With the default profile its output matches the lab's MATLAB converter (tdc_autoconverter, which writes d_txy_forc<N>.txt) byte for byte.

The <tag> in the name says which detector profile made the file, so TXY made with different profiles never get mixed up. HeLab never modifies a raw file, and never replaces a TXY that is already in a source folder.

docs.title: Ways to convert
docs.text:
• While Live watches a folder: turn on Auto-convert, and each new raw file is converted once it has finished being written. See Follow a folder live.
  • Any folder, any profile: right-click the folder › Convert this folder…, or File › Convert “<folder>”… for the tab's selected folder. Pick the profile (built-in or yours) and where the TXY go: HeLab's cache, its temp folder, or beside the raw files (on a share, HeLab asks first). Only that folder is converted, not its subfolders, and not while Live's Auto-convert is converting it.
  • From Folder details, for a folder on a network share that has raw files and no TXY at all: Folder details shows a Convert row, No TXY · on a share · Convert…. Click it and choose Convert to HeLab's cache (recommended), Convert to HeLab's temp folder or Convert beside on the share…. The row then shows the progress, for example Converting to HeLab's cache folder… 3 of 40, and the folder loads again when it is done. Files still being written after a few passes are left to Live's auto-convert.
  • Without the app, from a terminal: helab convert --watch FOLDER. See Command line.

A raw file is converted only once it has been unmodified for the settle time (Settings › General › Read files unmodified for, 5 s by default) and looks the same at two checks in a row. A raw file that stays unchanged for 20 s and still fails the format checks is called damaged: it gets no TXY, and later shots carry on. A shot whose raw file holds no hits gets an empty TXY (0 bytes), so "converted, empty" is never mistaken for "not converted yet".

docs.title: Where the TXY go
docs.text:
Settings › TXY converter › HeLab's TXY go to chooses:

Choice Where The disk cache's folder (the default) A converted-txy folder inside HeLab's cache folder, filed under the folder's data root. A folder without a .helab-root (see Mark a data root), or set to Don't cache, goes to the temp folder instead. HeLab's temp folder A converted-txy folder inside HeLab's temp folder.

These TXY don't count toward the disk cache budget, and nothing removes them except Settings › Cache › HeLab's converted TXY › Clear…, which asks first. See The disk cache.

docs.title: Beside the raw files
docs.text:
To write the TXY into the source folder itself, next to the raw files, turn it on for that folder: Live line › Auto-convert menu › Write TXY beside the raw files in this folder…. HeLab asks first, and the choice is saved for that folder only. It needs the disk cache and a confirmed .helab-root for the folder.

Beside the raw files HeLab writes only the d_txy_helab_<tag>_<N>.txt files. Each is written under a temporary hidden name and then renamed, so other programs never see a half-written TXY. HeLab never replaces a file already there.

Scripts that read raw folders

A lab script that lists d*.txt in a raw folder also sees HeLab's TXY written beside the raw files. Make such scripts match d<N>.txt exactly.

If the folder's file system can't add a file without risking replacing one, HeLab doesn't write there and asks: Retry, Write to HeLab's cache folder instead, Write to HeLab's temp folder instead, or Not now. A cache or temp choice holds for that folder until HeLab quits.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A detector profile holds every constant the conversion uses. Settings › TXY converter › Conversions use the profile picks the one HeLab's conversions use; the default is matlab-2019. The built-in profiles are read-only:

Profile Tag What matlab-2019 (default) m19v1 The lab's MATLAB converter, unchanged since 2017. matlab-2023-lab-edit m23v1 The 2023 lab edit of the MATLAB converter (an x1 dead time, other time sums). plates-2017, plates-2022 p17v1, p22v1 One per set of MCP plates; the same output as matlab-2019 until calibrated. plates-2025 p25t1 The same, marked uncalibrated.

The list under Profiles shows each one's notes, content hash and file name. Duplicate… makes your own copy, which you can Edit…, Export… or Delete… (asked first); Import… adds a profile JSON file. Your profiles are JSON files in HeLab's app folder (Show folder opens it), and their TXY are tagged u followed by 32 hex digits of the profile's content hash. Changes to profiles are saved at once; the choices at the top of the tab are saved with the dialog's Save.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text:
Settings › TXY converter › Backend chooses the code that does the conversion. Every backend writes the same TXY byte for byte; they differ only in speed.

  • numpy is the default and always available.
  • cython is an optional compiled backend. When running HeLab from source, build it with python native/build.py (it needs a C compiler); HeLab works without it.
  • reference is a plain-Python version kept as the yardstick: correct but slow.
  • The other entries are optional backends that need extra software installed.

A backend that can't run on this computer makes the conversion say why.

docs.title: Which TXY HeLab reads
docs.text:
To be written

HeLab reads each shot from the first entry of an ordered list that has a usable TXY: HeLab's TXY of a profile, or External (MATLAB converter), the MATLAB converter's d_txy_forc<N>.txt. Settings › TXY converter sets the list; this section will describe how to set it for a folder or a plot.

docs.title: Mark a data root (.helab-root)
docs.text: HeLab keeps loaded data in a disk cache so that a folder opens at once next time. It does that only for folders inside a data root: a folder holding a small hidden file named .helab-root. This page shows how to place one and what changes when you do.

docs.title: Why a data root
docs.text:
Without a .helab-root in the folder or any folder above it, the folder uses RAM only: its data, status and settings last for this session and are gone when you quit. Folder details then shows, on its Disk cache row:

RAM only · no .helab-root found here or above

The marker gives a drive or share an identity of its own. HeLab recognises the data by that identity, not by the path it is mounted at, so the same data is the same cache entry whether a computer reaches it as /Volumes/Data, D:\ or a network share.

docs.title: Where to put it
docs.text: Put the marker as high as possible: the top folder of the drive or share the data is on. Every computer that uses that drive then sees the same marker. Put it lower only if that lower folder is also shared on its own, so that other computers see it as a top folder.

docs.title: Place it
docs.text:
1. Right-click the folder in the tree and choose Place .helab-root here…, or use File › Place .helab-root in “<folder>”… for the current tab's selected folder (at first its top folder, which you can't right-click: for example the top of a drive).

  2. HeLab checks the folder first and warns when it:

    • isn't the top of its drive or share: it offers Place at <top> as well as Place here;
    • is already inside another data root;
    • is a home folder (such as /Users, /home or C:\Users);
    • is the top of the startup disk, or the folder of mounted drives (/Volumes on macOS).

    With any warning, Cancel is the default button, so pressing Return writes nothing. On Windows, writing at the top of the system drive may need administrator rights; HeLab says so. 3. Confirm. HeLab writes the hidden file, and the folder's modified date changes once.

If the folder already has a valid .helab-root, HeLab uses it. It never overwrites a file it can't read as a marker.

No write permission? HeLab opens Place the data-root file manually with the file's exact contents. Use Copy, or Save to folder… to write .helab-root under its exact name into a folder you choose, then move it into place and use Retry / Refresh on that folder. The file is hidden because its name starts with a dot: press Cmd+Shift+. in Finder, turn on View › Show › Hidden items in File Explorer, or press Ctrl+H in most Linux file managers.

docs.title: What you see afterwards
docs.text:
• The folder shows a blue anchor badge beside its status icon.
  • Folder details' Disk cache row names the marker in use, for example ⚓ Data · /Volumes/Data/.helab-root.
  • Right-click options that need the disk cache (Don't cache this folder, Don't auto-load this folder, Clear loaded data cache) become available for its folders.

The label shown is the folder's name when the marker was made (a drive letter for a Windows drive's top).

docs.title: Nested roots
docs.text: A data root may sit inside another. Each folder uses the nearest .helab-root at or above it. When you place one inside an existing root, HeLab warns that the inner folder gets its own identity, and its subfolders' cached data moves to it.

docs.title: Moved or copied data
docs.text:
If HeLab finds the same .helab-root at a second location (another share or server name, a different mapped drive, or a copied disk), it asks Same folder or a copy?:

  • Same folder: both locations share one disk cache.
  • It's a copy…: you pick which location keeps the cached data; the other gets a new .helab-root and starts with an empty cache.
  • Later asks again the next time HeLab finds that location this session; Remind me next session stays quiet until then.

Until you answer, the new location uses RAM only. Its folders show an amber triangle beside the status icon, the status bar shows "⚓ N to confirm", and the line under the path box offers Review… to answer.

Inside a root, cached data follows each folder's path below the marker. A folder you rename or move within the root is cached afresh.

docs.title: Settings › Data roots
docs.text:
In Settings (the Settings button in the left toolbar, or File › Settings...), the Data roots tab lists every .helab-root location HeLab has seen on this computer, with columns Data root, Status, Last seen and Cached (the size cached below it on this computer). Select a row to see the marker's full path and its ID. Rows for drives that aren't mounted are marked Not mounted.

For the selected row:

  • Show in Finder (File Explorer, File Manager) and Copy path (right-click the row).
  • Clear cached data…: removes what this computer cached below that root. The marker, folder flags and cached analysis stay.
  • Clear cached analysis…: removes only the saved analysis results below that root.
  • Forget location…: forgets this location. If its .helab-root is still there, the next listing finds it again.
  • Delete .helab-root…: deletes the marker file. The folder and its subfolders then use RAM only on every computer that uses this drive, until a marker is placed again; a new marker starts with an empty cache.
  • Review…: answers "Same folder or a copy?" for a waiting row.

Every one of these asks before it changes anything, with Cancel as the default.

See also: How HeLab caches data.

docs.title: Follow a folder live
docs.text: Live watches one folder while the experiment runs: each new shot joins the folder's data as soon as its file is written, and the plots of that folder run again on the newest shots.

docs.title: Turn Live on
docs.text:
1. Select the folder in a tab and let its data show.
  2. Click Live in the toolbar.

Live is also available for a folder that has no TXY files yet, before its first shot: select it once its listing has shown it is empty, and click Live. The tab then shows data with no shots, and the folder summary says waiting for the first shot.

Live is unavailable while the folder is still loading, while its cached data doesn't match the folder (use Review… first), and while working offline (File › Work Offline). Hover over the Live button to see why it is greyed out.

Live reads only the folder's own files, never its subfolders'.

docs.title: While Live is on
docs.text:
• The left panel collapses, giving its room to the plots. Live off, or an error, brings it back. If you had collapsed the panel yourself, it stays collapsed; open it with View › Toggle Left Panel.
  • The tab is locked: its folder tree, path bar and Deselect, and the toolbar's Up Dir, Refresh and Check folder status can't be used, so the watched folder stays selected.
  • The folder summary's third line shows Live's state, for example Live · checked 2s ago · 12 new shots · 1 still being written · next check in 3 s. Its tooltip has the details: checks so far, how long the last one took, and what isn't saved yet.
  • The status bar says Live: watching <folder> · N new shots.

docs.title: How shots arrive
docs.text:
• One check at a time. The next check starts a fixed time after the previous one ends: Settings › General › Live: check again after (3 s by default, 0.5 to 600 s). While the folder hasn't changed, a check costs one look at the folder, so a slow drive isn't loaded down.
  • Files still being written are left alone. A new file is read only once it has been unmodified for the settle time (Settings › General › Read files unmodified for, 5 s by default) and looks the same at two checks in a row. The line counts the others as still being written.
  • New shots stay in RAM and are shown at once. Every 10 new shots (by default), and when Live stops, HeLab saves the folder to the disk cache in the background. Change the number with Settings › Cache › Live: save to the disk cache every (1 to 100,000 new shots). A folder that HeLab can't cache (no .helab-root, see Mark a data root, or a folder set to Don't cache) keeps its new shots in RAM only, and the line says why.
  • A shot that changes soon after Live read it (within 5 minutes) is read again, and the line says so for a minute. An older shot that changes, shots that disappear, or another folder now at the same path stop Live as a mismatch: the data no longer matches the folder.

docs.title: Plots following Live
docs.text:
Each plot of the watched folder reruns on the newest data. In the plot's settings, the Live group decides when:

Setting What it does Follow Live On (the default): the plot reruns as new shots arrive. Off: the plot is pinned at the data it shows; turning it on again catches up. Rerun every N new shots Wait until this many new shots have arrived since the data of the last run. Wait after a run Rerun no sooner than this many seconds after the last run ended.

Each analysis starts from its own defaults (the hover text on each setting names them), and a plot never cancels a run in progress for new data. Shots that arrive meanwhile wait; the next run uses the newest data, skipping the steps in between, so no backlog builds up. The plot's source line shows the state: following Live · 3 new shots waiting, or pinned (Follow Live off) · 5 newer shots.

When Live stops (Live off, another tab, an error), every plot still holding shots back runs once more at once, whatever its Live settings, so each plot ends up on the latest data.

Some plots have Highlight the newest shot in their settings, which marks the latest shot in its own colour (red by default).

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: If a check fails (the drive is unreachable, a mismatch, a save error), Live stops checking but stays on and keeps the data: the folder summary line turns amber, reads Live stopped: <why>, and offers Retry. Nothing retries by itself. Retry checks the folder again and carries on; turning Live off instead saves the new shots it already has.

docs.title: Auto-convert while Live is on
docs.text:
Live can also convert the folder's raw files (d<N>.txt) to HeLab's TXY as they arrive. Click Auto-convert on the folder summary's Live line, or in the toolbar below Live (it stays there while the left panel is collapsed). Before Live starts, the same button reads Arm auto-convert: Live then converts from the moment you turn it on in that folder.

  • Each Live check also converts the raw files that have finished being written, using the profile and backend in Settings › TXY converter. The new shots join the data at the next check.
  • Auto-convert is remembered for the folder until HeLab quits; Live started afresh in another session starts with it off.
  • The Live line counts converted shots, shots still waiting, and damaged raw files (unchanged for 20 s and still failing the format checks). A damaged file gets one desktop notification, no TXY, and never holds up later shots. Shots converted with no hits are named in amber.
  • A raw file whose read stopped early (at a line that isn't numbers, where MATLAB's converter stops too) is named in amber, d3.txt read stopped at line 1010, and gets one desktop notification: its TXY holds only the hits before that line.
  • The arrow beside Auto-convert opens its menu: Write TXY beside the raw files in this folder…, Start Live and auto-convert here when HeLab launches, and Notify when a converted shot has fewer than 100 hits… (a desktop notification once per shot; 0 turns it off).
  • A conversion error stops auto-convert, not Live: the line turns amber and Retry converts again.

See Convert raw files to TXY for where the TXY go and what the profiles are.

docs.title: Start Live when HeLab launches
docs.text:
From the Auto-convert menu, Start Live and auto-convert here when HeLab launches makes this folder the launch folder. One folder only: choosing another replaces it. At the next launch HeLab opens that folder alone, in one tab, turns auto-convert on and starts Live once its data shows (or at once if it has no shots yet). If the folder can't be opened, a desktop notification says so and HeLab doesn't retry. Working offline, the tab opens without Live.

Apart from that, Live never restarts by itself after HeLab quits.

docs.title: Turning Live off and quitting
docs.text:
Live turns off when you click Live again, switch to another tab, or close the tab. Its new shots are then saved to the disk cache in the background.

When you quit while saves are running, a Saving before quitting window lists each one with how long it has run, and closes by itself when they finish. Quit now quits without waiting: the shots not yet saved stay in their files, and the next look at the folder reads them again.

docs.title: Write an analysis script
docs.text: An analysis script is a Python file with a class that derives from DatasetAnalysis. HeLab lists it in the Scripts panel; clicking one of its actions runs it on the data the current tab shows and draws the result in a new plot.

docs.title: Load and reload your scripts
docs.text:
Keep your scripts in a folder of your own, anywhere on your computer.

  1. In the Scripts panel, click Load Scripts... and choose the folder.
  2. Pick your script's group in the Group drop-down. Each script is listed with a button for each of its actions (the first two).
  3. Select a folder in a tab and let its data show, then click the action's button.

HeLab imports every .py file directly in the folder (not its subfolders), in name order. One file may hold several scripts. A file with no script in it that your scripts import is a helper module: put shared code there and import it as usual. Your scripts can also import the packages HeLab itself runs with, such as NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib.

HeLab remembers the folder and loads it again at each start, once the window has shown. A folder on a network share, or one HeLab was loading when it last stopped, waits for Reload instead, and an amber line under the buttons says so.

After you edit a script, click Reload: HeLab imports the folder's scripts and helper modules again, and open plots of them run again on the new code. If any of their runs is still computing, the button reads Reload (waiting) until it ends. To reload whenever you save a file, turn on Reload when a script is saved in the menu on the arrow beside Load Scripts.... That menu also lists your script folders, each with Reload and Remove from the list.

A file that doesn't load is listed at the end of the scripts, under ⚠ N script files didn't load: hover over its line for the traceback, or double-click it for a window with the details. Fix it and click Reload. A plot whose script didn't reload keeps running the code loaded before, and says so in amber.

Before HeLab imports a folder (at start, on Reload and from Load Scripts...), it test-imports the folder in a separate process, so a script that hangs or crashes at import can't stop HeLab; meanwhile the button reads Reload (checking). A folder whose test import doesn't finish within 10 s, or ends the process, isn't imported: it is listed with the reason, for example didn't load: its import didn't finish within 10 s. Code at the top level of your script runs twice (once in the test, once for real), so keep it to imports and definitions, and do the work in the script's methods.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
This script plots the mean arrival time (T) of each shot's events against shot number:

"""Mean arrival time per shot: an example HeLab analysis script."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, List, Optional

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QWidget

from helab.analysis.backends import MatplotlibPane, matplotlib_pane
from helab.analysis.follow import LivePolicy
from helab.analysis.parameters import ParameterSpec
from helab.analysis.results import AnalysisContext, AnalysisResult
from helab.analysis.selection import SHOT_SPECS, select_shots
from helab.scripts.base import DatasetAnalysis, ScriptMetadata

MIN_EVENTS = ParameterSpec(
    "min_events", "Minimum events", "int", 10, (1, 1_000_000), group="Mean T",
    tip="Shots with fewer events than this are left out.")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MeanT:
    shots: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
    mean_t: npt.NDArray[np.float64]  # seconds after the trigger
    skipped: int


class MeanArrivalTime(DatasetAnalysis):
    def get_metadata(self) -> ScriptMetadata:
        return self.create_metadata(
            name="Mean arrival time",
            description="Mean T of each shot's events, against shot number",
            group="My scripts",
            file_path=__file__,
            analysis_id="mylab.mean_arrival_time",
            version="1",
        )

    def get_actions(self) -> List[str]:
        return ["Plot"]

    def parameters(self, action_name: str) -> List[ParameterSpec]:
        return [*SHOT_SPECS, MIN_EVENTS]

    def live_policy(self, action_name: str) -> LivePolicy:
        return LivePolicy(every_shots=5)

    def compute(self, action_name: str, context: AnalysisContext) -> MeanT:
        # Worker thread: no Qt here, and the view's arrays are read-only.
        minimum = int(context.parameters[MIN_EVENTS.name])
        shots: list[int] = []
        means: list[float] = []
        skipped = 0
        for shot in select_shots(context.view, context.parameters):
            context.check()  # stops here if the user cancelled the run
            events = context.view.shots[shot]  # (n, 3): T in s, X and Y in m
            if len(events) < minimum:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            shots.append(shot)
            means.append(float(events[:, 0].mean()))
        return MeanT(np.array(shots, dtype=np.int64), np.array(means, dtype=np.float64), skipped)

    def render(self, result: AnalysisResult, parent: Optional[QWidget] = None) -> QWidget:
        # GUI thread: build the plot from what compute returned.
        figure = Figure(layout="constrained")
        draw(figure, result)
        return MatplotlibPane(figure, parent)

    def update(self, widget: QWidget, result: AnalysisResult) -> bool:
        # A rerun (e.g. Live's next shots) redraws in place, keeping the user's zoom.
        pane = matplotlib_pane(widget)
        if pane is None:
            return False
        pane.redraw(lambda figure: draw(figure, result))
        return True


def draw(figure: Any, result: AnalysisResult) -> None:
    data: MeanT = result.data
    axes = figure.add_subplot()
    axes.plot(data.shots, data.mean_t * 1e3, "o-", markersize=3)
    axes.set_xlabel("Shot number")
    axes.set_ylabel("Mean T (ms)")
    note = f" · {data.skipped} shots below the minimum" if data.skipped else ""
    figure.suptitle(f"{result.input.short()} · {len(data.shots)} shots{note}", fontsize=9)

What each part does:

  • get_metadata names the script. name is what the Scripts panel and the plot show, group the section it is listed under. analysis_id is a stable ID that never changes, even if you rename the script; bump version whenever the output changes. Every result records both, with a hash of the script's file.
  • get_actions lists the actions, each a button in the Scripts panel. HeLab passes the action's name back to every other method as action_name.
  • parameters declares the plot's settings, shown in the Settings panel. A ParameterSpec gives the key, the title, the kind ("float", "int", "bool", "choice" or "text"), the default, and optionally limits, a unit suffix, a tooltip and a group (its section). In compute, context.parameters holds a value for every parameter you declared, checked and clamped to its limits.
  • compute does the numerical work and returns anything render can draw; a small dataclass works well. It reads the data only from context.view, a DatasetView: view.shots maps each shot number to its events, an (n, 3) array of T (s after the trigger), X and Y (m), in ascending shot order. view.events(shots) joins chosen shots into one array.
  • render builds the plot's widget from the result; result.data is what compute returned. MatplotlibPane shows a Matplotlib figure with its toolbar.
  • update (optional) shows a newer result in the plot already drawn. Return False to have render draw it anew instead.

Your script isn't an importable module

HeLab runs a script's file rather than importing it, so after loading it isn't in sys.modules: typing.get_type_hints() can't resolve a script class's string annotations (those from __future__ import annotations makes). Dataclasses work either way.

docs.title: Threads and shared data
docs.text:
• compute runs on HeLab's analysis worker thread. Don't create or touch Qt widgets there, and don't read files or watch folders: everything the run needs is in context.
  • render and update run on the GUI thread. Keep them quick: do the heavy work in compute.
  • The view's arrays are shared and read-only. HeLab and other plots use the same arrays, and NumPy refuses to write to them. Call .copy() on an array before changing it.
  • Let a long run stop. Call context.check() between steps or in long loops: it ends the run when the user cancels it. Or test context.cancelled() and return early.
  • Use Matplotlib's matplotlib.figure.Figure, never pyplot.
  • Errors don't stop HeLab. If compute or render raises, the plot says it failed and why (a plot already showing a result keeps it, with the error above it); if another method raises, HeLab logs it and goes on.

docs.title: Choose shots with the shared Shots settings
docs.text: Adding SHOT_SPECS from helab.analysis.selection to your parameters gives your plot the same Shots section as HeLab's own plots: all shots, the last N or a range of shot numbers, from a first shot. select_shots(context.view, context.parameters) returns the chosen shot numbers in ascending order, and HeLab records them as the shots the run used.

docs.title: Follow Live
docs.text:
While Live watches a folder, its plots run again on the newest shots. A run is never cancelled for new data: shots that arrive meanwhile wait, and the next run takes them all. By default a plot runs again on every new shot. A slow analysis can ask for fewer reruns from live_policy: LivePolicy(every_shots=5, min_delay=10.0) reruns once five new shots have come, and no sooner than 10 s after the last run ended. Each plot's Live settings (Follow Live, Rerun every N new shots, Wait after a run) start from your policy and can change it.

context.live is True for a rerun that follows Live, so a costly analysis can do less then. A view can have no shots at all (Live started before the folder's first shot), so make sure compute and render handle empty data.

docs.title: More in the API reference
docs.text:
The API for script writers documents every hook and helper:

  • the script contract: DatasetAnalysis, ScriptMetadata and the optional hooks, such as describe_run (the plot's source lines), minimum_size and parameter_warnings;
  • the dataset view: DatasetView and its shot times;
  • run context and results: AnalysisContext and AnalysisResult;
  • parameters: ParameterSpec, including SI units and settings that show only under one choice;
  • shot selection: the Shots, View range and newest-shot settings;
  • fits: the fit helpers HeLab's own plots use.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
HeLab installs one command, helab. Without a subcommand it starts the app; helab convert and helab cache run in the terminal, without the GUI.

Command What it does helab Start the HeLab app. helab --version Print the version and build information, then exit. helab convert --watch FOLDER … Convert a folder's raw files to TXY, without the GUI. helab cache dump FILE.hlb Print a disk cache file's header. Read only. helab cache export … Export disk cache files to NumPy, MATLAB or CSV files. Read only.

python -m helab works the same as helab, with the same subcommands and options. In the packaged app, run the executable inside it with the same arguments: HeLab.app/Contents/MacOS/HeLab convert … on macOS, HeLab.exe convert … on Windows. The Windows app has no console, so its lines go only to the log file.

docs.title: helab
docs.text:
helab                                   # start the app
helab --version                         # print the version and build information
helab --geometry 1600x1000+0+0          # this run's window size and position

--geometry WxH+X+Y sets the main window's size and the top-left corner of its frame, for this run only.

One HeLab app per computer. If HeLab is already running, a second start shows HeLab is already running on this computer … Use its window, or quit it before starting HeLab again. and exits with code 1. helab convert and helab cache don't count: they run beside the app.

docs.title: helab convert
docs.text:
helab convert --watch FOLDER [--once] [--profile NAME|FILE.json] [--backend NAME]
              [--output temp|cache|cache-forced|beside|beside-forced]
              [--workers N] [--interval SECONDS] [--again]

Watches a folder and converts its raw files (d<N>.txt) to HeLab's TXY files (d_txy_helab_<tag>_<N>.txt) as they finish being written. It uses the same converter, rules and output folders as the app (see Convert raw files to TXY), runs without the GUI, and can run while the app is open. Its log goes to the terminal and to HeLab's log folder (Help › Show log folder in the app).

The first check only records each raw file; a file is converted once it is unchanged between two checks. Ctrl-C stops it between two writes: every TXY is written under a temporary name and then renamed, so none is left half-written.

Option Meaning --watch FOLDER The folder of raw files. Required. --once Convert what is there now, then exit. Only files unmodified for a minute are read; the rest are reported as still waiting. --profile NAME or FILE.json A built-in detector profile's name, or a profile JSON file (for your own profiles, use the file). Default matlab-2019. --backend NAME The converter backend: numpy (default), cython, reference, or numba, mlx, rust where installed. --output temp Write the TXY to HeLab's temp folder. --output cache Write them to HeLab's cache folder. For a folder set to Don't cache, it warns and asks Write to the cache folder anyway? [y/N]; without a terminal, or on no, the temp folder. --output cache-forced The cache folder, even for a folder set to Don't cache, without asking. --output beside Write the TXY next to the raw files, for this run, whatever the folder's own setting. On a network share it asks first (below). --output beside-forced Beside the raw files even on a network share, without asking. The share's warning is still logged. --workers N Processes converting at once. Default: half the computer's cores, at most 4 (1 in the packaged app). --interval SECONDS Seconds between checks of the folder. Default 3. --again Convert every shot once more, current ones too (cache and temp folders only).

Without --output, the TXY go where Settings › TXY converter › HeLab's TXY go to says (the cache folder unless you changed it). A folder without a .helab-root, or set to Don't cache, goes to the temp folder.

Beside the raw files on a network share, --output beside warns once and asks Write the TXY beside the raw files on the share anyway? [y/N]. No, or no terminal, converts to HeLab's own folder instead, and the log names --output beside-forced, which writes beside without asking. (Older versions had --yes for this; it is now a usage error naming beside-forced.)

If the share can't take a file safely (its file system can't add a file without risking replacing one), it asks [r]etry, write to HeLab's [c]ache or [t]emp folder instead, or [q]uit? [r/c/t/Q]. A cache or temp answer holds for the rest of the run. Without a terminal nothing is written beside, and the log suggests --output cache or --output temp.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Follow a run's folder, converting each new shot into HeLab's cache folder
helab convert --watch "/Volumes/Data/2026/run 1"

# Convert what is there now with another built-in profile, then exit
helab convert --watch "/Volumes/Data/2026/run 1" --once --profile matlab-2023-lab-edit

On Windows, for example on the acquisition computer, writing the TXY beside the raw files:

helab convert --watch D:\data\run1 --output beside

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Done, or stopped with Ctrl-C. 1 With --once, the conversion failed; or you answered quit after a refused write beside the raw files. Without --once, a failed check is logged and the next one goes on. 2 A usage error, a folder that doesn't exist, or a profile that can't be read.

docs.title: helab cache
docs.text:
helab cache dump FILE.hlb
helab cache export FILE.hlb [--to npz|mat|csv] [--out PATH] [--bin-time SECONDS] [--force]
helab cache export --folder FOLDER [--kind raw|txy] [--layer LAYER] [--cache DIR]
                   [--to npz|mat|csv] [--out DIR] [--bin-time SECONDS] [--force]

Looks into the .hlb files of HeLab's disk cache and exports them. It is read only: it never writes into the disk cache or a source folder, never replaces a file without --force, refuses an --out inside the disk cache, and works while the app is running. The file format is described in HeLab's .hlb files.

docs.title: dump
docs.text: helab cache dump FILE.hlb checks the whole file and prints its header as JSON: what the file is, which HeLab made it, and each array's name, type, shape and compressed size.

docs.title: export
docs.text: Option Meaning FILE.hlb Export one file: a raw layer (one raw file's pulses: columns channel, time_bins, time_s), or a TXY segment (columns shot, t_s, x_m, y_m). --folder FOLDER Instead of a file, export what the disk cache holds for this source folder. The folder needs a .helab-root at or above it. --kind raw or txy With --folder: raw pulses (default), one file d<N>.<ext> per shot; or TXY, one file d_txy<N>.<ext> per shot, columns t_s, x_m, y_m. --layer LAYER With --kind txy: which TXY to export, matlab, a profile tag such as m19v1, or helab:<hash>. Needed when the folder has more than one. --cache DIR The cache folder to read. Default: the one HeLab uses. --to npz, mat or csv NumPy .npz (default), MATLAB .mat, or CSV with one row per pulse or hit. .npz and .mat files also carry the header, as JSON text. --out PATH The output file (one file) or folder (--folder). Default: the current folder for one file, ./helab-export-<folder name>/ for a folder. --bin-time SECONDS Seconds per TDC bin, for raw layers' time_s. Default 25e-12. --force Replace output files that already exist.

docs.text:
# What is in this file?

# Every cached raw file of a run, for MATLAB
helab cache export --folder "/Volumes/Data/2026/run 1" --to mat

# The cached TXY of the matlab-2019 profile, as CSV
helab cache export --folder "/Volumes/Data/2026/run 1" --kind txy --layer m19v1 --to csv

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open the Settings window with File › Settings... or the Settings button on the left toolbar. It has six tabs: General, Lab parameters, TXY converter, Scripts, Cache and Data roots.

The buttons at the bottom:

  • Save keeps your changes and closes the window. Changes to converter profiles and the actions on the Cache and Data roots tabs (Clear, Remove, Forget and so on) take effect at once, without Save.
  • Cancel closes the window without saving.
  • Reset all settings… puts every setting back to its default, after asking: folders, load options, both cache budgets, window and view choices, and the list of plots to reopen. The cache folder's location, the disk cache's contents and your presets are kept. While you work offline, it asks whether to keep working offline or go online.

docs.title: API for script writers
docs.text:
These pages document the classes and functions an analysis script uses, generated from HeLab's own docstrings. To get started, read Write an analysis script first.

Page What it covers Script contract DatasetAnalysis, the class a script derives from, and ScriptMetadata Dataset view DatasetView, the read-only data a run gets, and its identity Run context and results AnalysisContext, what compute gets, and AnalysisResult, what render draws Parameters ParameterSpec, the settings a script declares Shot selection and view range The Shots, view range and newest-shot parameters every plot can share Fits Least-squares fits of histograms and the T/X/Y profile fits

Everything here is plain Python with no Qt, so a script's compute and its tests run without a display. Arrays a run receives are shared and read-only: call .copy() before changing one.

docs.title: Dataset view
docs.text:
A DatasetView is the one input an analysis gets: compute reads it as context.view. It is a read-only, immutable snapshot of the data a folder tab has loaded. Its arrays are shared with HeLab and with other runs, and NumPy refuses writes to them: call .copy() before changing one.

Each shot is an Events array of shape (n, 3): T in seconds since the trigger, and X and Y in metres. events(shots) joins chosen shots into one new array; txy gives a shot's T/X/Y columns.

While HeLab follows a folder live, each batch of new shots makes a new revision of the view (revision, added_shots), with the same identity (identity).

A read-only, immutable snapshot of a loaded dataset: the one input an analysis gets.

compute reads it as context.view. Its arrays are shared with HeLab and with other runs, and read-only: copy one (.copy()) before changing it. A view may have no shots (Live started before the folder's first shot); a plot then says it is empty.

Attributes:

  • identity (ViewIdentity) –

    Which data this is (ViewIdentity).

  • revision (int) –

    1 for a loaded dataset, one more each time a newer load (Live's) adds or replaces shots, or only finds their raw files' times.

  • shots (Mapping[int, Events]) –

    Shot number → that shot's events, a read-only (n, 3) T/X/Y array (Events), in ascending shot order. events joins chosen shots into one array.

  • fingerprints (Mapping[int, Fingerprint]) –

    Shot number → its TXY file's Fingerprint.

  • provenance (Provenance) –

    Where the data came from (Provenance).

  • data_root (DataRootRef | None) –

    The data root the folder is under, when known.

  • added_shots (tuple[int, ...]) –

    The shots this revision added or replaced (a replaced shot's array is new: its TXY file was rewritten, or it now comes from another TXY). A revision that only found shot times has none. A running total over revisions must take a replaced shot's old events out before adding its new ones.

  • created_at (float) –

    When the view was made (wall-clock time).

  • dataset_signature (str) –

    The signature of the loaded dataset this revision is ("": the identity's, as at revision 1).

  • raw_times (Mapping[int, int]) –

    Shot number → its raw d<N>.txt file's mtime in ns, where one was found (shot_time reads it).

  • origins (Mapping[int, str]) –

    Shot number → its origin, helab:<profile hash>, for shots read from HeLab's own TXY; shots from MATLAB's TXY aren't listed.

  • txy_profiles (Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]) –

    Profile hash → its name, version and whether it is calibrated, for the HeLab TXY in the view.

  • on_read (frozenset[int]) –

    The HeLab shots converted from their raw files when they were read.

  • fallback (frozenset[int]) –

    The shots read from beyond the TXY choice's own list, because none of its entries had them: from its fallback (the folder's or Settings' list, External, then any HeLab TXY). origins says which TXY each is.

  • txy_choice (str) –

    The TXY choice the data was loaded with ("": none named, MATLAB's TXY alone). Views of two choices are never revisions of each other.

docs.title: helab.analysis.fits
docs.text:
Bounded least-squares fits of 1D histograms, for the T/X/Y fits of the DLD port.

fit_histogram(centres, counts, model) fits one of the registered MODELS with scipy.optimize.curve_fit and returns a FitResult: each parameter's value ± SE (from the covariance), the model curve, χ² per degree of freedom and, when the fit can't be trusted, a failure reason. Failures (no data, too few points, everything in one bin, no convergence, an undetermined parameter) are results with a note, never exceptions, so a plot can say why it shows no fit.

How a fit runs: - Input: raw counts per bin, or anything else with its errors given as sigma= (rates, smoothed counts). The count weights assume whole-number counts and say so otherwise. - Weights: counts are Poisson. weights="poisson" (the default) first fits with each bin's error √max(n, 1), then refits with the model's own variance until the parameters settle: the Poisson maximum-likelihood fit (_reweight says why: the first fit alone biases widths low). "counts" stops after the first fit. Either way the covariance is absolute (the SEs don't scale with χ²; a poor model shows as a large reduced χ², noted). "none" fits unweighted and scales the covariance by the residuals instead. - Offset: for counts (nonnegative_offset; by default raw counts with count weights) a model's offset is at least 0 (a mean count can't be negative), and an offset at 0 isn't noted as "at its bound"; otherwise (sigma= rates, background-subtracted data) it keeps the model's bound, −top. - Bins: by default (binned) the model is averaged over each bin (five-point Gauss–Legendre, bin_means), not taken at its centre: a centre value biases a width by about +w²/(24σ) for bins w wide (Sheppard's correction: +0.5 SE at 50 000 events in bins of σ/5, several SE at 10⁵–10⁶). Bin edges are edges= when given, else halfway between neighbouring centres, which assumes equal-width bins of counts. binned may be a weight function w(x) (r² for radial shells): each bin then gets ∫w·f / ∫w. The result's curve and evaluate are the model itself at points (not averaged), for drawing. - Scaling: x and counts are mapped to order one before fitting (a T profile is ~0.4 s wide ~0.1 ms, counts ~10³), each parameter by its role (a position, a width, a height or a dimensionless shape), and mapped back with the covariance. - Starting points come from moments (each model's guesses); a model may give several, and the converged one with the lowest χ² is kept. - Components: a parameter that only shapes one part of a model (a TF radius) names that part's amplitude as its gate. When the amplitude is consistent with 0 (within 2 SE) the fit says so in a note and the parameter's SE is nan, instead of failing.

Models are derived from the physics, not copied from the MATLAB code (which has bugs). Registered now: Gaussian + offset, the Thomas–Fermi projection (1 − u²)^p + offset, bimodal TF^p + Gaussian with a shared centre, and the exact arrival-time ("Yavin") thermal profile on T (arrival_time_model), and the Bose-enhanced thermal profiles g_{5/2} and g_2 (bose_model, with polylog) and the bimodal TF² + g_{5/2} and TF^{3/2} + g_2 (fugacity 1). condensate_fraction and component_areas give N0/N and the parts' areas ± SE from a fit's covariance; helab/analysis/bec.py turns them into BEC properties and sets the R/σ_th cap per axis. Pure NumPy/SciPy, no Qt. Fits run in the analysis worker thread, so nothing here changes warning filters per call (warnings.catch_warnings isn't thread-safe).

docs.text:
bin_means(

    lower: Array,
    upper: Array,

function(x, *values) averaged over each bin [lower, upper] by five-point Gauss–Legendre quadrature (exact for polynomials up to degree 9; for a Gaussian in bins of σ its error is ~10⁻¹⁰ of the peak, against the centre value's ~4 %). docs.title: fit_histogram
docs.text:
fit_histogram(
    centres: ArrayLike,
    counts: ArrayLike,
    model: str | FitModel = "gaussian",
    *,
    weights: Weights = "poisson",
    sigma: ArrayLike | None = None,
    max_evaluations: int = MAX_EVALUATIONS,
    max_radius_ratio: float = MAX_RADIUS_RATIO,
    covariance_of: Callable[[Array, Array, Array], Array]
    | None = None,
    nonnegative_offset: bool | None = None,
    binned: bool | Callable[[Array], Array] = True,
    edges: ArrayLike | None = None,
) -> FitResult

Fit model (a MODELS key or a FitModel) to a histogram's bin centres and raw counts. sigma, when given, is each bin's error (absolute) and replaces weights: pass it for anything that isn't raw counts. Bins with a non-finite centre, count or error, or an error ≤ 0, are left out (noted).

max_radius_ratio caps R/σ_th in models with a ratio parameter (bimodal; see bimodal_model for why 2, and when to raise it). A fit that ends at the cap says so; the cap goes in the result's options and record.

covariance_of(x, values, fitted), when given, replaces the fitted parameters' covariance (data units, from the weights alone) before anything reads it: the SEs, the "consistent with 0" gating and its notes, the undetermined check and the extras. For data whose bins are correlated (a smoothed curve: profiles.fit_smoothed), where only the caller knows the real spread; x are the bins fitted.

nonnegative_offset: the offset is at least 0 (counts); None means so for raw counts with count weights (no sigma, weights not "none"). binned: the model is averaged over each bin; False takes it at the centres (point samples, or a model that already integrates its bins); a function w(x) averages with that weight, ∫w·f / ∫w (radial shells: r²). edges (len(centres) + 1, in the centres' order) are the bins' exact bounds, used whenever given; without them the edges are halfway between the centres given (before any are left out), which is right for equal-width bins of counts only.

gaussian(

    amplitude: float,

∫ A exp(−(x − μ)²/2σ²) dx = A σ √(2π).

thomas_fermi_area(
    amplitude: float, radius: float, power: float = 2.0

∫ A (1 − u²)₊^p dx = A R √π Γ(p + 1) / Γ(p + 3/2) (16/15 A R at p = 2), without the offset.

docs.title: bimodal_model
docs.text:
bimodal_model(
    power: float, bose: float | None = None
) -> FitModel

A condensate on a thermal cloud, one centre: A_c (1 − u²)₊^p + A_t exp(−(x − x₀)²/2σ²) + offset, u = (x − x₀)/R, R = r σ with r = R/σ from MIN_RADIUS_RATIO up to the fit's max_radius_ratio. R is reported as an extra. Started from a Gaussian fit (count weights, or the caller's errors), split four ways (the last a cold cloud's, clipped to the cap).

bose (the polylog order, 5/2 or 2) makes the thermal part the Bose-enhanced A_t g_ν(e^{−(x − x₀)²/2σ²}) / ζ(ν), its fugacity fixed at 1 (see bose_thermal).

docs.text:
polylog(order: float, x: ArrayLike) -> Array

    amplitude: float,
    centre: float,
    sigma: float,
    fugacity: float,
    offset: float,
    order: float = 2.5,

docs.title: bose_area
docs.text:
bose_area(
    amplitude: float,
    sigma: float,
    fugacity: float,
    order: float = 2.5,
) -> float

∫ A g_ν(z e^{−u²/2σ²}) / g_ν(z) dx = A √(2π) σ g_{ν+1/2}(z) / g_ν(z) (1 as z → 0).

docs.text:
bose_model(order: float) -> FitModel

The Bose-enhanced thermal profile g_ν + offset, its fugacity z fitted in [0, 1]. Started from a Gaussian fit, at three fugacities (σ wider as z grows: the enhanced centre is narrower).

docs.title: condensate_fraction
docs.text:
condensate_fraction(fit: FitResult) -> Estimate

N0/N = A_TF / (A_TF + A_thermal) from a bimodal fit's component areas, ± SE by the delta method on the fitted parameters' covariance (so the areas' correlation is counted). nan for a failed fit or a model without a condensate part. The fraction is of the counts the histogram holds: a cropped box or window crops the thermal wings more than the condensate. On a slice model (FitModel.slice: TF^{3/2}, g_2) it is the slice's fraction, not the cloud's (a thin central slice holds relatively more condensate); the fit's notes say so (SLICE_NOTE).

docs.title: helab.analysis.profiles
docs.text:
T/X/Y profiles for the histogram plot: display units, rates per shot, Gaussian smoothing, and the fits with their temperatures.

The units and the rate method follow the MATLAB front panel's dld_plot_tof.m, with its bug fixed: - Axes: X and Y in mm, T in ms (display_units). - Rates: counts / bin width / number of shots, after the view range (and, when chosen, the whole box) has picked the events: T in kHz per shot (per ms), X and Y per mm per shot (the front panel divided X and Y by the bin width only). - Smoothing (optional): a Gaussian of σ over bins of σ/5 (the front panel's bin_factor). Fits use the unsmoothed counts unless the smoothed curve is chosen.

Fits are in the data's own units (s, m) on counts per bin; drawing scales the fitted curve by the same factor as the bars. No Qt and no I/O: runs in the analysis worker and in tests.

docs.title: Smoothing
docs.text:
Smoothing(bins: int, sigma_bins: float)

The smoothing of bins bins with a Gaussian of sigma_bins bins, as the linear map s = S n (a sparse matrix): each bin's counts spread by the kernel, the edges reflected (the bins beyond an edge mirror those inside, np.pad's "symmetric"), so what spreads past an edge folds back in and every column sums to 1: the total is kept. The same S smooths what is drawn and, in a fit of the smoothed curve, the model (fit_axis).

docs.title: mu_consistency
docs.text:
mu_consistency(
    axis: Axis,
    constants: ResolvedConstants,
    bin_width: float,
    shots: int | None,
) -> Consistency

fits.choose_condensate's check of a bimodal fit against the constants: μ/k_BT from its R/σ_th (R/σ = √(2μ/k_BT) λ(t_f)/√(1 + ω²t_f²) on this axis's trap axis: bec.radius_ratio_cap at μ/k_BT = 1 is √2 times that factor) against bec.from_fit's μ/k_BT from N0 and T, within fits.MU_AGREEMENT. Can't check (None, with why): no shot count, an axis between the trap's axes, or no μ from N0 (a slice, no condensate).

docs.title: fit_axis
docs.text:
fit_axis(
    axis: str,
    edges: ArrayLike,
    counts: ArrayLike,
    choice: str,
    constants: ResolvedConstants,
    smoothing: float | None = None,
    max_radius_ratio: float | None = None,
    shots: int | None = None,
) -> AxisFit

Fit one histogram (edges in s or m, raw counts) with the model choice names.

By default the raw counts, Poisson weighted (fit_histogram). smoothing (σ in the data's units) fits the smoothed curve instead, with the smoothing in the model (fit_smoothed): the parameters are the unsmoothed profile's, so the width (and a bimodal fit's R) needs no correction, and the SEs count the smoothed bins' correlation. Temperatures are the ideal-gas, pure-expansion ones (physics): along T σ_v = g σ, along X and Y σ_v = σ / t_f, each with the run's constants. max_radius_ratio: the bimodal fits' cap on R/σ_thermal (fit_histogram); None (the default) takes this axis's physical cap at μ/k_B T ≤ 2 (axis_cap: the trap frequencies, the fall time and which detector axis is the trap's long one), or fits.MAX_RADIUS_RATIO when those don't give one.

The bimodal TF + Bose choices also fit the free-z Bose profile and report a condensate only when that one saturates and the bimodal fit is clearly better (fits.choose_condensate); otherwise the result is the free-z fit, with "no condensate (z = …)" in the notes. With shots (the shots the histogram sums), an unsaturated case is also checked against the constants (mu_consistency). A smoothed-curve fit makes that decision on the unsmoothed counts (two more fits: correlated smoothed bins inflate Δχ² several times) and shows the smoothed fit of the model it chose.

docs.title: smoothed_model
docs.text:
smoothed_model(
    model: FitModel, smoothing: Smoothing, centres: Array
) -> FitModel

model with the smoothing applied to its prediction on the bins (centres), the model averaged over each bin (fits.bin_means): S·f̄(θ). Anywhere else (a finer grid, as FitResult.evaluate draws) it is the unsmoothed model: S belongs to those bins only.

docs.title: fit_smoothed
docs.text:
fit_smoothed(
    centres: Array,
    raw: Array,
    model: FitModel,
    sigma_bins: float,
    max_radius_ratio: float = MAX_RADIUS_RATIO,
) -> tuple[FitResult, Array]

Fit the smoothed counts s = S n with the smoothed model S f(θ) (smoothed_model), and the smoothed fit's curve on the bins.

  • Weights: each smoothed bin's variance from the model, Σⱼ Sᵢⱼ² μⱼ with μ = f(θ) (floored as fits.VARIANCE_FLOOR per raw bin), refitted up to SMOOTHED_ROUNDS times until θ settles. The first fit uses the observed counts' (S² n); weights from observed counts alone would bias low-count fits.
  • SEs: the smoothed bins share raw counts, so their covariance is S diag(μ) Sᵀ, not diagonal. Each fit's covariance is the sandwich (JᵀWJ)⁻¹ JᵀW S diag(μ) Sᵀ WJ (JᵀWJ)⁻¹, with J the smoothed model's derivatives and W the weights: what the estimator's spread really is. It goes to fit_histogram (covariance_of), so the SEs, the "consistent with 0" gating and its notes, the undetermined check and the extras (a bimodal R) all use it.

Parameters an analysis declares: defaults, limits and units, validated before a run.

A choice parameter picks one of its choices and a text one holds free text the analysis reads itself (e.g. mask circles, masks); another parameter can say it applies only under one of them (when, and shown_with for a condition on several), so the parameter tree shows it only then and the dock's source line leaves it out otherwise. group names the tree section it sits in, and page the settings tab (a plot whose parameters name more than one page gets a tab each).

Example

Attributes:

    The key the analysis reads in context.parameters.

  • title (str) –

    What the plot's settings show.

  • kind (Kind) –

    The type (Kind).

  • default (Value) –

    The value when none is set.

  • limits (tuple[float, float] | None) –

    (min, max) a number is clamped to; None for no limits.

  • suffix (str) –

    The unit shown after a number (e.g. " %", " s").

  • tip (str) –

    The tooltip in the plot's settings.

  • choices (tuple[str, ...]) –

    The run's ID.

docs.title: helab.scripts.base
docs.text:
The script contract: the base classes every HeLab analysis script derives from.

A script is a Python file whose class derives from DatasetAnalysis (an analysis of one loaded dataset) and names itself with ScriptMetadata. HeLab lists its actions in the Scripts panel; running one calls compute on the analysis worker thread with an AnalysisContext (the read-only DatasetView and the effective parameters), then render on the GUI thread to draw the result in a plot dock. Every other method has a default, so a script overrides only what it needs.

This module imports no Qt at run time (tests/test_headless_imports.py): a script's compute and its tests run without a display.

docs.title: DatasetAnalysis
docs.text:
Bases: HelabAnalysisScript

An analysis of one loaded dataset.

The Scripts panel runs an action on the current tab's dataset view: compute gets an AnalysisContext (the immutable view and the effective parameters, never the tab) and runs in the analysis worker thread, so it must not touch Qt widgets. render then builds the plot dock's content from the result on the GUI thread. Arrays in the view are shared and read-only: copy one before changing it.

A plot of the folder Live watches follows it: HeLab reruns it on each newer revision of the view, as the script's live_policy allows. A script never reads files or watches folders itself, and a view may have no shots yet (Live started before the first one): its plot then shows that it is empty, not an error.

Metadata must give analysis_id and version. Parameter values are plain JSON values (numbers, booleans, strings).

An analysis that uses physical constants adds constant_layers.constants_specs(keys) to its parameters: the plot's settings then show each constant's value and source, and can set it for that plot. Each run gets the lab and folder layers in context.constants and, resolved with the plot's own values when it was submitted, context.resolved_constants, which its result records; compute reads them there, never from the table's defaults. An analysis with its own override parameters declares constant_keys and run_constants instead.
